title: Sandstone Erosion Layers with Cross-Section Reveal
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that renders an interactive sandstone formation with visible erosion layers and a cross-section reveal mechanic.

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Add a DirectionalLight at (5, 10, 5) intensity 1.2, plus AmbientLight intensity 0.3.
- Background color: #87CEEB (sky blue).
- Add a ground plane (20x20) with a sandy color (#C2B280).

## Sandstone Formation
- Create a sandstone column/mesa as a group of 6 horizontal layer meshes stacked vertically.
- Each layer is a CylinderGeometry(radius ~2.5, height ~0.5) representing a geological stratum.
- Layer colors from bottom to top: ['#8B4513','#A0522D','#CD853F','#DEB887','#D2B48C','#F5DEB3'] (dark to light, representing oldest to youngest).
- Each layer material should use MeshStandardMaterial with roughness varying per layer: [0.95, 0.9, 0.85, 0.8, 0.75, 0.7] (bottom roughest).
- Position layers so they stack: layer 0 at y=0.25, layer 1 at y=0.75, etc.

## Erosion Simulation
- Implement an erosion system controlled by a slider (HTML range input, id='erosionSlider', min=0, max=100, step=1, default=0).
- Erosion value 0 = pristine formation, 100 = fully eroded.
- As erosion increases, each layer's radius shrinks. Top layers erode faster than bottom layers.
- Layer i effective radius = baseRadius * (1 - erosionFactor * (1 + i*0.15)), where erosionFactor = sliderValue/100.
- Clamp each layer's scale to minimum 0.0 (layer disappears). Top layers should vanish first.
- When a layer's effective scale drops below 0.05, set it invisible (visible=false).

## Cross-Section Reveal
- Add a 'Cross-Section' toggle button (id='crossSectionBtn').
- When active, use a clipping plane (THREE.Plane) on the X axis to cut the formation in half, revealing internal layers.
- The clipping plane normal should be (1, 0, 0) with constant 0, applied to all layer materials via material.clippingPlanes.
- Enable renderer.localClippingEnabled = true.
- Toggle state: clicking the button alternates between clipped and unclipped views.

## Layer Selection
- Implement raycasting: clicking on a layer highlights it with emissive color (#FFD700, intensity 0.3) and displays layer info.
- Only one layer can be selected at a time. Clicking empty space deselects.
- Display selected layer info in a HUD div (id='layerInfo') showing: layer index, geological name, age (in millions of years), and current erosion percentage for that layer.
- Geological names bottom to top: ['Basal Conglomerate','Iron-Rich Sandstone','Cross-Bedded Sandstone','Fine Sandstone','Siltstone','Caprock'].
- Ages bottom to top: [250, 220, 180, 150, 100, 65] (millions of years).

## Wind Direction Control
- Add keyboard controls: pressing 'W','A','S','D' changes wind direction which biases erosion.
- Wind direction affects erosion asymmetry: when wind is active, layers scale non-uniformly (scaleX vs scaleZ differ).
- 'W' = north wind (reduces scaleZ more), 'S' = south wind (increases scaleZ bias), 'A' = west wind (reduces scaleX more), 'D' = east wind (increases scaleX bias).
- Wind bias factor: 0.2 additional erosion on the windward axis.
- Display current wind direction in a HUD element (id='windDisplay').
- Default wind: 'None'.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- erosionLevel: current slider value (number 0-100)
- layerCount: number of currently visible layers (0-6)
- layerRadii: array of 6 current effective radius values
- layerVisibility: array of 6 booleans
- crossSectionActive: boolean
- selectedLayer: index of selected layer or -1
- selectedLayerName: string name or ''
- selectedLayerAge: number or 0
- windDirection: string ('None','North','South','East','West')
- windBias: {x: number, z: number} representing current wind erosion bias
- cameraPosition: {x,y,z}
- layerRoughness: array of 6 roughness values
- totalVisibleVolume: sum of all visible layer radii (as a proxy for volume)

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.

## HUD Layout
- Top-left: erosion slider with label showing percentage.
- Top-right: cross-section button.
- Bottom-left: layer info panel (id='layerInfo').
- Bottom-right: wind direction display (id='windDisplay').
- Style all HUD elements with semi-transparent dark backgrounds, white text, rounded corners.
physics_constraints: Erosion must be monotonically increasing from bottom to top layers (top layers erode faster). Layer radii must be non-negative. When erosion=0, all layers must have base radius. When erosion=100, at minimum the top 2 layers must be invisible. Wind bias must not cause negative scale values. Total visible volume must decrease monotonically as erosion increases.
